title: Workshop Rota

source.name: Original exercise inspired by Harold W. Kuhn's The Hungarian Method for the Assignment Problem

statement:
A community repair workshop needs a rota for its open day. It has `n` volunteers and `n` workstations. Every volunteer can staff any workstation. Pairing volunteer `i` with workstation `j` adds `c[i][j]` to the workshop's budget. A negative value represents a credit.

Assign each volunteer to exactly one workstation and staff each workstation with exactly one volunteer. Find the minimum possible total cost.

**Input.** The first line contains the integer `n`. The next `n` lines each contain `n` signed integers. In row `i`, the `j`-th integer is the cost `c[i][j]`.

**Output.** Print one integer, the minimum total cost.
hints: Treat volunteers and workstations as the two sides of a complete bipartite graph. The cheapest choice in each row can send several volunteers to the same workstation.
Give each row a potential u[i] and each column a potential v[j], with u[i] + v[j] <= c[i][j]. What lower bound follows when you sum this inequality along a full assignment?

Use the Hungarian algorithm. From each new row, grow an alternating tree and remember the smallest slack to each unreached column. Adjust the potentials by the smallest of those slacks until the tree reaches a free column.
editorial:
Let `u[i]` and `v[j]` be row and column potentials satisfying `u[i] + v[j] <= c[i][j]`. Initialise `u[i]` to the minimum cost in row `i` and `v[j]` to zero. This works for signed costs. Every full assignment costs at least `sum(u) + sum(v)` because it uses every row and column once. An edge is tight when `c[i][j] - u[i] - v[j] = 0`. A perfect matching made of tight edges attains the lower bound.

Process the rows one at a time. Start an alternating tree at the new row. Each reached occupied column adds its matched row to the tree. For each unreached column, store its smallest slack from any reached row and the predecessor column that gives that slack. Take `delta` to be the smallest stored slack. Raise the potentials of reached rows by `delta` and lower the potentials of reached columns by `delta`. Slacks within the tree stay fixed, slacks into it from outside increase, and slacks out of it decrease by at most their current value. Feasibility and matched-edge tightness are preserved, and at least one new column becomes reachable by a tight edge. When the search reaches a free column, follow the predecessors and flip the matching along that path.

After all rows are processed, sum the costs of the matched pairs. Each of the `n` searches visits at most `n` columns and scans `O(n)` entries per visit, giving `O(n^3)` time. The matrix uses `O(n^2)` space and the auxiliary arrays use `O(n)`. The total can have magnitude `120 * 10^9`, so use 64-bit integers in C++ and Java. JavaScript numbers represent the required integers exactly.

starter.python:
import sys

tokens = iter(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = next(tokens)
cost = [[next(tokens) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]

solutions.python:
import sys

tokens = iter(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = next(tokens)
cost = [[next(tokens) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]

# Column 0 is a sentinel whose owner is the root of the current search.
u = [0] + [min(row) for row in cost]
v = [0] * (n + 1)
owner = [0] * (n + 1)
columns = range(1, n + 1)

for row in columns:
    owner[0] = row
    column = 0
    used = [False] * (n + 1)
    slack = [float("inf")] * (n + 1)
    previous = [0] * (n + 1)
    while True:
        used[column] = True
        current = owner[column]
        costs = cost[current - 1]
        row_potential = u[current]
        delta = float("inf")
        next_column = 0
        for j in columns:
            if used[j]:
                continue
            reduced = costs[j - 1] - row_potential - v[j]
            if reduced < slack[j]:
                slack[j] = reduced
                previous[j] = column
            if slack[j] < delta:
                delta = slack[j]
                next_column = j

        if delta:
            u[row] += delta
            for j in columns:
                if used[j]:
                    u[owner[j]] += delta
                    v[j] -= delta
                else:
                    slack[j] -= delta
        column = next_column
        if owner[column] == 0:
            break

    while column:
        parent = previous[column]
        owner[column] = owner[parent]
        column = parent

print(sum(cost[owner[j] - 1][j - 1] for j in columns))
